# Original Nivo BoxPlot color, legend and hover reference

This fixture executes complete Nivo 0.99.0 `useLevels`, `useBoxPlot`, `getLegendData`, and `useBoxPlotTransition` bodies, plus their original ordinal/inherited color, summary and scale functions. The original source files and MIT licenses are preserved under `vendor/`, with commit and byte hashes.

Run `node scripts/box-colorby-hover-reference.mjs <released-D3-node_modules>` to generate, or append `--check` to verify. It uses Node TypeScript erasure and released D3 scale 4.0.2, interpolate 3.0.1, array 3.2.5 and color 3.1.0. It does not install dependencies. No Babel/TSX, mounted React lifecycle, Spring animation, original legend component or pixel rendering is exercised.

`values.json.profiles` has 32 inputs: group/subGroup color identity, authored/reversed full category order, four source shapes, and default/explicit `group` legend-label property. Each profile contains complete raw observations, full palette, baseline, activation using a genuine previously computed item, and verified restoration. The hook itself prewarms the full group/subgroup palette, including reserved empty keys; the actual D3 ordinal domain is recorded. Both nonempty legend configurations invoke the original helper and preserve its numeric IDs, labels, colors and order. It deduplicates labels and only includes actual boxes. `sourceKey` is an adapter annotation mapping the original numeric index back to the input domain; it is not a native field.

`baseline` and `active` contain original computed boxes and transition outputs. `activeKeys` is the actual original `useMemo` return, captured by its unique original dependency pair; it is not reconstructed by a replacement hover algorithm. The relation is group OR subgroup and is independent of colorBy. Ten qualification snapshots retain empty data, upstream filtering, foreign/stale active identity, malformed JavaScript active objects, an explicit callback label, null coercion, and overlapping group/subgroup names.

Rust comparison boundaries remain explicit: Rust omits `None`, whereas native `Number(null)` contributes zero and can create a null-only box. Native computed keys are numeric index pairs; Rust keys preserve typed group/subgroup identity. A changed native numeric key with unchanged identities is ignored by the native relation and is not an overrideable field on the Rust key. Foreign identities can partially match natively but are rejected by bounded Rust lookup. The new Group legend can match native default-label items after translating numeric IDs to raw keys. Legacy Rust SubGroup legends keep the full configured domain, including empty slots; this fixture does not silently change that default. Custom legend labels/property paths are recorded native behavior, not a claim of a new Rust accessor API. Alpha-zero numeric palette RGB is preserved; no modifier/parser compatibility changes or native Contrast equivalence are claimed.

Adapters are limited to immediate memo evaluation, supplied cold state, primitive-label deduplication and stable numeric sorting, ordinary dotted property lookup/functions, and linear/band scales. Other retained original scale/scheme branches explicitly reject execution. All expected colors, legends, keys and opacities are actual original function outputs, not pixels or source-derived substitute algorithms.
